newsitem.title: UK: Hanson pre-demerger profits top forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Hanson pre-demerger profits top forecasts.

text.p: British conglomerate Hanson Plc reported annual pretax profits of 1.8 billion pounds ($2.92 billion) on Thursday, the last set before the demerger process kicked off in October, with chairman Lord Hanson predicting that the outlook for the former "family of companies" was very good.

But the chairman also warned that the recent share price performance had been "very disappointing" and said "This in no way represents either our earning capacity or future prospects." The pre-demerger results showed profits topping forecasts and were up sharply from 1.22 billion last year.
The profits included a one-off gain of 609 million pounds, compared with a 98 million charge last year. Earnings per share were 25.6 pence versus 18.2 pence and a dividend of one pence will be paid.
The main focus of interest was the update for the two remaining building and energy divisions, after Millennium Chemicals and Imperial Tobacco were spun off on October.

Energy is next on the list to be demerged. Hanson said in its results statement that the energy unit is seen demerging in February. The date of the shareholder meeting to gain approval and further details will be announced shortly.

Looking at trading conditions for the two remaining businesses, the UK operations continue to suffer from tough housing and construction markets. But some signs of a turnaround are evident. Buoyant U.S. conditions continue. Energy enjoyed a "substantial" rise in profits "showing significant growth overseas and a further increase in UK profit and market share." ($1=.6161 Pound)
